title: Decision-tree depth bound from a computing tree
statement: Let $f : (\mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \mathrm{Bool}) \to \mathrm{Bool}$ be a Boolean function, and let $T$ be a decision tree on $n$ variables of depth at most $d$ that computes $f$, meaning $T$ evaluates to $f(x)$ on every input $x$. Then the decision-tree depth of $f$ is at most $d$.
hypotheses_covered: T is a decision tree on n variables
depth of T is at most d
T evaluates to f(x) for every input x
replaced:
If a decision tree $T$ of depth at most $d$ computes $f$ (i.e.\ $T.\mathrm{eval}\,x = f(x)$
for all $x$), then the decision-tree depth of $f$ is at most $d$.
